openai_navier_stokes.title: Finite Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes
openai_navier_stokes.theorem_as_reported: There exist a smooth, compactly supported force f and a time T such that the solution u of the forced 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on R^3, starting from rest, is smooth on [0, T) and sup|u| becomes unbounded as t -> T, while the kinetic energy stays uniformly bounded for all t < T.
openai_navier_stokes.forcing: smooth, compactly supported in space and time
openai_navier_stokes.energy: L^2 norm uniformly bounded for t < T
construction_components_as_reported: a self-similar concentrating axisymmetric vortex, shrinking to a point in similarity coordinates as t -> T
small-scale spatially-localised oscillatory pulses in a cylindrical annulus, whose Reynolds stress cancels the momentum residual
an iterative correction scheme removing higher-order residuals while preserving compact support of f

the_finding.headline: The programme's target statement was answered externally, by an apparatus outside the programme's search space, while the programme's own recorded ceiling remained Tier 2 and its own recorded odds remained 0.05%, unmoved.

the_specific_miss.claim: Leg 381 found the door and closed it. It correctly refuted 'f = 0' for statement (C) and correctly called the forcing 'a genuine relaxation'. It then inferred that the relaxation 'buys no escape from the decay and bounded-energy obligations'. On the external record's reported construction, the forcing is EXACTLY what buys the escape: the oscillatory pulses' Reynolds stress absorbs the momentum residual that the localisation problem (W4) otherwise leaves on the solution, and the force is kept COMPACTLY SUPPORTED, which discharges Fefferman condition (5) at no analytic cost rather than at the cost leg 381 priced.
the_specific_miss.status: UNVERIFIED. This is a reading of third-party summaries of a manuscript this repository has not audited at full text. It is banked as the first unit of the next arc to check, NOT as a landed finding.
the_specific_miss.why_it_is_worth_banking_anyway: lesson 76 -- the negative construction stays in the artifact. A wrong inference that closed the winning door is the single most informative row this repository can carry, and it is exactly the kind of row a programme is tempted to smooth over.

structural_reasons_the_plan_could_not_ha: CEILING. Tier 3 needs CLAY_OBLIGATIONS.md section 6 items 1 and 2. Both have no known method. Leg 314 classified item 2 as of a kind computation cannot supply. The programme's own documents say the ceiling is Tier 2.

SEARCH SPACE. The genome is initial data. The external construction starts from REST -- u0 = 0. Its entire content lives in a force the genome has no gene for. No fitness landscape over u0 contains that object, at any budget, for any number of generations.
LADDER POSITION. The banked pipeline is 1D gCLM at Tier 2; 2D Boussinesq was Phase 1; 3D Euler is Stage 4, unscheduled. The target equation was several unscheduled rungs above the last landed one.
APPARATUS. Tier 3 here was to be a Newton-Kantorovich radii-polynomial contraction, scoped by C1. The external proof uses no interval arithmetic, no DNS and no search: it is analysis, then Lean.

COMPUTE WAS NEVER THE BINDING CONSTRAINT. W7 was measured from the inside at leg 403: 79.1% of a step is transforms, the best priced fix is 3.41x, and the wall's own note reads 'a speedup breaks no wall, and no link moved.'
what_this_does_NOT_establish: It does not establish that the external proof is correct. It is unrefereed, its Lean review is self-assessed, independent verification is incomplete, and a priority dispute is unresolved.
It does not establish that the Clay problem is resolved. CMI's four conditions are unmet, the two-year clock has not started, and OpenAI has said it will not claim the prize.
It does not close statements (A), (B) or (D). (A) and (B) are the unforced problem and are untouched. (D) is the torus.
It does not retroactively make any Tier-2 result in this repository a proof. Tier 2 is never a proof. That rule is unchanged by anything in this file.
